title: Choose the visual world for Showrun
question: The roll assigned Run of Show. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Layout, navigation and controls stay standard shadcn app UI in every option; the world only sets type, palette, density and one signature move.

options.label: Run of Show
options.lineage: TV broadcast rundown sheets and colored script revisions
options.thesis: Every run is a live rundown: items in order, timed, and nothing irreversible goes to air without your cue.
options.viewport: Left: the run's rundown table (no., item, outcome, time drawn to scale), the live row lit by a tally-red time marker; right: the step's before/after screenshots and the STANDBY cue card when approval is needed.
options.risk: Broadcast language can tip into theme if words like ON AIR leak into labels; labels stay plain English.

raised.raise: Step durations are drawn to exact scale in the time column, so slow steps and model calls are visible at a glance.
A pending approval owns the whole work area with the evidence large; A approves, R rejects, the next item is already loaded.
Status is carried by glyph shape and a word, never by hue alone.
One strict 4px grid and one column system across all four pages; nothing sits off it.

options.label: Stamped and Received
options.lineage: Philippine office rubber stamps: RECEIVED, APPROVED, with date and initials
options.thesis: Your approval is a stamp: dated, initialed, permanent on the item it cleared.
options.viewport: Run table on the left; each approved item carries a small violet date-stamp mark with time; the pending card asks for your stamp.
options.risk: Highest local resonance, but a stamp texture done badly reads as kitsch on a working screen.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white, one accent, and every outcome sits next to the screenshot that proves it.
options.viewport: Item list, then a detail pane where each decision is paired with its before/after frames.
options.case: Clearest product read of all; loses on identity, since it looks like every well-made dev tool.
options.risk: Polished but generic; judges may not remember it.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: The run is a live board: items rerank in place and a changed row stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: A dark board of run items with status and time columns; heals and learned answers hold amber until acknowledged.
options.case: Strong on live state; dark board fights the light mock apps beside it in the video.
options.risk: Can read as a travel-app costume if the board styling goes past type and color.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State as line height and dash on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with every destination as a tick.
options.case: An ops person does not recognize a spectrogram; state encoding is too abstract for approvals.
options.kept: Status never relies on hue alone.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Action blocks whose length is exact duration.
options.viewport: A vertical score of steps read upward.
options.case: Nobody in the audience reads dance notation.
options.risk: Pure costume on a working screen.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen, next one a flick away.
options.viewport: One screenshot full-bleed with glyph actions.
options.case: Hides the run overview an ops person needs.
options.kept: The pending approval owns the work area, next item preloaded.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A grid poster with monumental type.
options.case: A poster, not a tool; no fit for approvals.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean automation dashboard: sidebar, tables, a detail drawer, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, runs table, detail pane.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
